## open_stream  (streaming)
Open a stream: a named table whose latest rows live in memory, written many times a
second by a script (``s = await stream.open(name)`` then ``await s.write(row)`` in
run_code) with no tool call per write. A dashboard's chart or table bound to the
returned view_uri updates by itself, only while someone is looking. window keeps the
last N rows (1: the latest only; at most as many rows as one view reads); the rows are
saved as the artifact's next version every flush_s seconds while they change and when
the stream stops. columns names the columns a view can bind to before the first write.
A background script's streams stop when it ends; their last rows stay readable and
show as stopped.

open_stream(name: string, columns?: any, window?: integer, flush_s?: number)
Open a stream: a named table whose latest rows live in memory, written many times a
second by a script (``s = await stream.open(name)`` then ``await s.write(row)`` in
run_code) with no tool call per write. A dashboard's chart or table bound to the
returned view_uri updates by itself, only while someone is looking. window keeps the
last N rows (1: the latest only; at most as many rows as one view reads); the rows are
saved as the artifact's next version every flush_s seconds while they change and when
the stream stops. columns names the columns a view can bind to before the first write.
A background script's streams stop when it ends; their last rows stay readable and
show as stopped.

cron_create(max_fires?: integer, until?: string, cron?: string, prompt?: string, recurring?: boolean, run_at?: string, delay_s?: integer, timezone?: string)
Schedule a future turn for THIS session (recurring cron or one-shot).

Give exactly ONE trigger:
- ``cron``: a 5-field expression ("min hour day-of-month month day-of-week",
  e.g. "0 9 * * *" = 9am daily, "*/15 * * * *" = every 15 min, "0 9 * * 1-5" =
  weekdays 9am). Evaluated in the session's LOCAL timezone.
- ``run_at``: an ISO-8601 instant to fire ONCE ("2026-08-01T09:00").
- ``delay_s``: fire ONCE after this many seconds.

``prompt`` is the question the scheduled turn will run. ``recurring=False`` (or any
``run_at``/``delay_s``) makes it a one-shot that deletes itself after firing.
``timezone`` overrides the session default (an IANA name like "America/Chicago").
max_fires and until are optional explicit user limits; zero/empty are unlimited.

Returns a dict with the server-generated ``schedule_id`` (use it with cron_delete),
the resolved ``cron``/``timezone``, ``recurring``, and the ``next_fire_at`` UTC
instant. Call cron_list first if unsure whether you already armed this — do not
double-arm. A bad cron or an anti-runaway clamp trip raises a typed error to repair.

input.code:
import asyncio
import json
import math

rows = json.loads(open("burn.json", encoding="utf-8").read())
sensor = await stream.open("burn-observations", columns=["local_label", "particle_mean_ug_m3"],
                           window=18, flush_s=30)
simulation = None
theta, velocity, simulation_time = 0.1, 0.0, 0.0
for i, row in enumerate(rows):
    await sensor.write(local_label=row["local_label"], particle_mean_ug_m3=row["particle_mean_ug_m3"])
    if i == 40:
        simulation = await stream.open("pendulum-simulation", columns=["time_s", "angle_rad"],
                                       window=18, flush_s=30)
    if simulation is not None:
        for _ in range(30):
            acceleration = -9.80665 * math.sin(theta)
            theta += velocity * 0.01 + 0.5 * acceleration * 0.01**2
            velocity += 0.5 * (acceleration - 9.80665 * math.sin(theta)) * 0.01
            simulation_time += 0.01
        await simulation.write(time_s=round(simulation_time, 3), angle_rad=theta)
    await task.progress("Replaying recorded observations", done=i+1, total=len(rows))
    await asyncio.sleep(0.6)
await task.notify("Sensor replay complete")
print("Sensor replay complete")
